title: Gaussian-process-assisted engineering of a ketoreductase for an ipatasertib precursor
summary: A six-round engineering campaign combined mutational scans, structure-guided libraries and Gaussian-process models. The model-aided library yielded M3, reported with 22-fold higher apparent activity than wild type in the UV assay. Three subsequent conventional mutagenesis rounds produced M6, a 10-substitution descendant with 64-fold higher apparent kcat, but also about 12-fold higher apparent KM; do not attribute M6 as a direct model output or treat kcat as production yield. The authors report a 100 g/L laboratory process test with ≥98% conversion and 99.7% diastereomeric excess after 30 hours. These are process-relevant laboratory results, not a commercial production run or drug efficacy.
organization: Institute of Chemistry and Biotechnology, Zurich University of Applied Sciences; F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd.

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full article, methods/results, publication history, affiliations and chronology of model and conventional rounds.

evidence.tested: M3 and later M6 were tested for activity; article reports preparative reactions at 100 g/L substrate and conversion/stereoselectivity under specified laboratory conditions.
evidence.unknown: M6 follows conventional site-mutagenesis rounds after the AI-informed step; apparent kcat differs from process yield and KM changed; no commercial production/clinical efficacy claim.
evidence.ai_role: Gaussian-process predictions informed smaller follow-up variant libraries within a broader workflow that also used mutational scanning, rational design and conventional evolution.
